result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers meet every rubric item: body size and leading fall in range, line length is capped, .note gets bigger but stays secondary, colors and HTML are untouched, and the heading hierarchy is sound. A edges ahead because it caps and centers the whole .page column, so lists and notes get the same readable width. B caps only the p elements and leaves other content running edge to edge, though its text-wrap additions are a nice touch. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers meet every rubric item. Each sets body text at 17–18px with 1.55–1.6 line-height, caps line length near 65–68ch, raises .note to 13–14px, keeps the colors and HTML, and keeps a clear heading order with tighter but reasonable heading line-heights and 1em paragraph spacing. A adds text-wrap refinements and caps only paragraphs, while B centers a capped column and suggests a specific darker gray for the contrast issue, so neither is clearly better.
